subject: BrightMesh onboarding: request to consolidate PO issuance and reassign spend caps
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@brightmesh.io>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: BrightMesh onboarding packet (forms + SKU list)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick heads up during the vendor intake call earlier. Attached is our completed onboarding packet and an export of our legacy SKU mapping (BrightMesh_sku_legacy_map.xlsx). I noticed the procurement form has a field for 'primary tax id' and we included both our US EIN and a VAT reference for completeness — happy to confirm whichever you need on file.

A couple of notes that might impact PO issuance: our platform uses two legacy SKU families that accounting still references (BM-CORE and BM-ADDON). If those map to separate ledger codes on your side, we may see split POs or provisional tokens. For a pilot phase we'd prefer a single consolidated PO with a spend cap set at $45,000 for Q2 to simplify billing.

Please let me know if you need an amended form or additional authorization to consolidate.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Finance, BrightMesh
Attachments: BrightMesh_onboarding_form_v2.pdf, BrightMesh_sku_legacy_map.xlsx
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-05-01T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: BrightMesh onboarding packet (forms + SKU list) — PO issuance guidance required

Team — forwarding BrightMesh's packet. Quick summary: vendor provided two legacy SKU families; onboarding form lists both EIN and VAT; vendor requests single PO with $45k spend cap for the quarter. Our intake system sometimes splits to provisional POs when multiple ledger codes are detected (we've had this exact issue before).

Action items:
- Monica: can we issue a provisional PO now to unblock the vendor and then consolidate to a single canonical PO once we confirm ledger mapping?
- Priyom: can you check whether the legacy SKUs will trigger multi-PO issuance in the onboarding pipeline and whether we can force a single purchase-reference on this account?
- Aditya: if we need to make an SLA exception for a consolidated PO (manual election), please advise on approvals and whether finance needs a memo.

Vendor is asking for a single PO to avoid split billing. I think a provisional PO + follow-up reconciliation would work but don't want to leave them in limbo.

Thanks — Kimberly
Procurement Ops | Redwood Inference
From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-05-01T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: BrightMesh onboarding packet — PO issuance guidance required

Kimberly / team,

Thanks. I pulled the intake logs for BrightMesh and confirmed our provisioning flow created two provisional POs overnight: PO-123456 (BM-CORE ledger) and PO-123457 (BM-ADDON ledger). Each carries a provisional spend cap of $25k and $22k respectively — so they total $47k, slightly above the vendor's requested $45k.

Options:
1) Consolidate to a single canonical PO and retroactively reassign ledger lines. This requires manual reconciliation and a short memo to finance (Aditya) for spend alignment.
2) Leave as two provisional POs and ask BrightMesh to sign a combined master invoice approach (not ideal for them).

Recommendation: issue a provisional consolidate ticket, create a single canonical PO (PO-123490 placeholder), and adjust ledger mappings so that BM-ADDON lines map to the BM-CORE master code during the pilot. I can prepare the memo and manual journal entries once we have approvals.

I've attached the two provisional stubs for reference (PO_123456_stub.pdf, PO_123457_stub.pdf).

Monica
Senior Procurement Manager | Redwood Inference
Attachments: PO_123456_stub.pdf, PO_123457_stub.pdf
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@brightmesh.io>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: finance@brightmesh.io
Date: 2025-05-02T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightMesh onboarding — PO consolidation request

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for digging in. We can confirm that BrightMesh is comfortable with a single PO for the Q2 pilot and can accept your recommended approach (consolidate and remap BM-ADDON to BM-CORE for the pilot). We prefer a single PO number to ensure our billing system doesn't split invoices.

Next steps from our side: we'll sign a short addendum confirming the spend cap of $45,000 and authorizing the ledger remap for the pilot. I've routed a DocuSign for that addendum (link below).

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/recipient/0a1b2c3d

Please let us know the canonical PO number once created and any memo language finance needs.

Best,
Elena
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@brightmesh.io>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-05-02T14:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightMesh onboarding — PO consolidation request (PO-123490 issued)

Elena — thanks for the quick turn. We went ahead with option 1 and created a canonical PO for the pilot: PO-123490. 

What we did:
- Created canonical PO-123490 with spend cap $45,000 (pilot Q2).
- Flagged PO-123456 and PO-123457 as provisional and scheduled automated closure once journal reassignments complete.
- Reassigned BM-ADDON lines to map under the BM-CORE master ledger for the duration of the pilot.
- Finance (Aditya) will post a short reconciliation memo into the vendor file and handle the manual crediting between provisional POs and PO-123490.

Attachments: PO_123490_stub.pdf (issued). Expect a confirmation email from finance with the reconciliation memo and a final copy of the DocuSign addendum after BrightMesh completes signing.

If anything changes on your side (e.g., you need a different spend cap split), flag it here and we can adjust.

Kimberly Park
Procurement Ops | Redwood Inference
Attachments: PO_123490_stub.pdf
